key_insight: LLIFT generates semi-synthetic brain MRI with realistic, spatially controlled lesions using only image-level labels or bounding-box guidance, enabling ground-truth data for XAI evaluation without pixel-level lesion annotations.
clinical_relevance: This could improve benchmarking of explainable AI in medical imaging by creating more realistic test images with known lesion locations, supporting safer model assessment workflows.
method: LLIFT-GAN: a custom GAN learns pathological features from binary healthy vs pathological labels.
LLIFT-DM: a diffusion inpainting pipeline uses ControlNet with bounding-box masks to place lesions in user-controlled regions.
Both produce semi-synthetic MRI benchmarks with controlled ground truth for downstream XAI testing.
evidence_signal: On Human Connectome Project-derived brain MRI, both variants achieved FID scores against real pathological images that were comparable to the healthy-versus-pathological reference gap, with qualitative inspection supporting lesion realism.
watch_item: The approach depends on how well semi-synthetic lesions match real pathology, so results should be validated carefully before using the datasets as a substitute for clinical ground truth.
paper_title: Local Label-Informed Feature Transfer for Generating Ground-Truth Medical Images: A Comparison of GAN- and Diffusion-Based Approaches
